title: Pointwise Minimax Dose-Response Rates and the Treatment-Density Smoothness Elbow
banked_reason: Independent referee re-grade: subfield, not field. Achievability is a first-order re-derivation of Bonvini-Kennedy (arXiv:2207.11825) on a strictly smaller region: Omega forces alpha <= 2 and is EMPTY at alpha=beta=1 for d >= 4, whereas their published oracle region s >= d/4 is satisfiable for every (alpha,beta,d). The matching converse is the textbook one-dimensional Tsybakov floor on a covariate-free submodel (p_X = pi = 1, mu constant in x), so it carries no causal content. The promised elbow is never proved (oeq:deficient-frontier remains open with a non-matching bracket and no exhibited coincidence region), and the all-beta floor re-proves the already-accepted bank entry stat_dose_response_minimax_holder_anisotropic_converse on a re-drawn class.
gap_reasons: The delivered sharp result is confined to the construction-dependent region Omega: there the note proves both the explicit estimator upper bound and the matching one-dimensional Le Cam lower bound, but it does not determine the interior frontier for 0<c<1 outside that region.

The beta-invariance theorem is correspondingly local to tuples whose rougher class lies in Omega and follows from class nesting plus those two rate bounds; it is not a global beta-invariance characterization.
The deficient-region result is only a nonmatching two-sided exponent bracket, and the c=1 theorem concerns a degenerate boundary where the treatment density is forced to be uniform.

K2 promised the exact order for every s >= d/4; Omega delivers strictly less. Omega forces alpha <= 2 (via the structural clause (alpha^1)+(beta^1) >= alpha) and is EMPTY at alpha=beta=1 for d >= 4, because the pilots in def:beta-free-handle are histograms and dose-window averages, so every exponent is capped at order 1.

The converse half (lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor) uses p_X = pi = 1 and mu constant in x, i.e. Tsybakov Ch. 2 with covariates, overlap, beta and s switched off; it is the easy half of the Bonvini-Kennedy conjecture, not the elusive one.

The all-beta floor re-proves the already-accepted bank entry stat_dose_response_minimax_holder_anisotropic_converse/thm:sharp-pointwise-lower-bound on a re-drawn class; nothing in the pipeline detected the collision.

The motivating 2beta/(2beta+1)-vs-2alpha/(2alpha+1) contrast is drawn against Bonvini-Kennedy's FIRST-ORDER bias term (their Eq. 7), which their own higher-order corrections in the same section exist to cancel; their published rate contains no beta at all.

Unverified proof step: in lem:localized-polynomial-master-risk (writeup.tex:1123-1127) the passage from the pointwise bias bound to the squared risk of the local-polynomial solution is asserted, not derived — random A-dependent weights are not handled. This is the single step the whole upper bound rests on.
proof_attempt_summary: Aimed to show the treatment-density smoothness beta is not a genuine hardness parameter for the pointwise dose-response minimax rate, by proving global beta-invariance (K1) and the exact order n^(-2alpha/(2alpha+1)) for all s >= d/4 (K2). What was delivered is an explicit first-order estimator whose risk matches a one-dimensional Le Cam floor only inside a construction-dependent region Omega that is strictly smaller than the promised s >= d/4 — it forces alpha <= 2 and is empty at alpha=beta=1 for d >= 4 — with beta-invariance correspondingly local and following from class nesting rather than from new mathematics. The promised elbow was never reached: outside Omega only a non-matching exponent bracket exists, with no exhibited region where its two endpoints coincide, and that remains the open kernel.
tldr: On the explicit separated-pilot oracle region \(\Omega\), the four-fold marginal local-polynomial estimator attains the pointwise minimax mean-squared-error rate \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\), matching a one-dimensional Le Cam lower submodel whose treatment density is uniform. When \(\beta<\alpha\), this exponent is numerically larger than the exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\) obtained from Bonvini and Kennedy's treatment-smoothing bias--variance balance: their \(h^\beta\) term is an absolute bias, so the MSE balance is \(h^{2\beta}\asymp(nh)^{-1}\). The comparison is between unlike guarantees and is not an estimator-domination claim.
gap: Existing continuous-dose results can display treatment-density smoothness in estimator-specific conditional risk bounds, while the fixed-dose partial-mean minimax frontier over nested anisotropic H\"older classes is not thereby determined. In particular, an absolute treatment-smoothing bias \(h^{\alpha\wedge\beta}\) contributes its square to mean-squared error. Outside the explicit region \(\Omega\), the exact frontier remains unresolved for \(0<c<1\), although the core records an optimized achievable bracket, an all-\(\beta\) oracle lower floor, and a stronger fuzzy lower bound in an extreme low-\(s\) region.
fill: The explicit Borel estimator has uniform risk at most a constant times \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\) on \(\Omega\), and a uniform-treatment two-point submodel gives the matching lower bound for every finite \(\beta\). Nested-class monotonicity then yields one-sided \(\beta\)-invariance comparisons whenever the rougher tuple lies in \(\Omega\). The paper reports the deficient-region upper and lower brackets honestly rather than promoting them to an exact rate.
